docs.summary:
Headset rendering and tracking through OpenXR.

While running, the first perspective [`Camera`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Camera) with no target texture and a [`StereoTargetEye`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Camera~StereoTargetEye) draws both eyes into the headset in one stereo view, using its transform as the head, and the window or Game View shows one eye. Put a [`TrackedPoseDriver`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.TrackedPoseDriver) on the camera so the head moves it, under a parent that places the play area in the world. The headset paces the frame loop while it shows frames, so VSync and [`TargetFrameRate`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Application~TargetFrameRate) are set aside meanwhile.

The graphics device has to be made for the headset, so set [`InitializeOnStartup`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XR~InitializeOnStartup) before the window opens.

members.name: InitializeOnStartup
members.signature: public static bool InitializeOnStartup { get; set; }

docs.summary: Makes the graphics device for the headset when the window opens, which XR needs before [`Start`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XR~Start) can work: it connects to the OpenXR runtime, which may start it, and uses the GPU and Vulkan extensions it asks for. Set it before the game runs. Off, XR costs nothing.
Whether the graphics device was made for the headset, so [`Start`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XR~Start) can connect.

members.name: RenderScale
members.signature: public static float RenderScale { get; set; }

docs.summary: Scale applied to the headset's recommended eye resolution when [`Start`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XR~Start) is called. Below 1 trades sharpness for speed.
A session is running, whether or not the headset is showing it yet.
The headset was lost and XR is waiting for it to come back, trying again every couple of seconds.
The headset is showing this application's frames.
The headset is showing this application and it receives controller input.
The origin poses are measured from, which can fall back to [`Seated`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XRTrackingOrigin~Seated) when the headset has no floor level space.
The resolution each eye renders at.
How many frames a second the headset displays, 0 when not running or not known yet.
Whether the headset can track bare hands. See [`IsHandTracked`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XRInput~IsHandTracked).
Whether the headset can track where the eyes look, through [`EyeGaze`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XRNode~EyeGaze).

Raised when tracking space moved under the player: after [`Recenter`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XR~Recenter), or when the headset's runtime recentres or redraws the play area itself. Poses jump on the frame this is raised.

Makes where the head is now the centre of tracking space, facing forward along it. With floor tracking the floor stays where it is, seated tracking also takes the head's height. Takes effect on the next frame.

members.name: TryGetPlayAreaSize
members.signature: public static bool TryGetPlayAreaSize(out Float2 size)

docs.summary: The width and depth of the play area the player set up, in metres, centred on the tracking space's floor origin before any [`Recenter`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XR~Recenter). False when the headset has no play area or does not report it.

members.name: Start
members.signature: public static bool Start(XRTrackingOrigin origin = XRTrackingOrigin.Floor)

docs.summary: Connects to the headset through the active OpenXR runtime. Returns false, and logs why, when there is no runtime, no headset, the runtime cannot render with Vulkan, or the device was not made for XR (see [`InitializeOnStartup`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XR~InitializeOnStartup)).
Ends the session, and stops waiting for a lost headset to come back.
The pose of a tracked device for the frame being displayed, in tracking space.
Whether `camera` already drew its eyes into the headset this frame.
Whether `camera` renders to the headset while XR runs: the frame wants drawing, the camera is a perspective one drawing to the screen with eyes to draw, and no other camera drew the eyes this frame.
The eye's pose relative to the head and its frustum, for this frame.

The two layer target the headset's eyes draw into this frame, the left display's image in layer 0. Drawing `camera` into it, through [`BuildView`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Camera~BuildView), is what sends the frame to the headset with the camera's pose. One camera draws the eyes per frame.
The texture behind [`GetEyeTarget`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.XR~GetEyeTarget), two layers, the left display's image first.

members.name: EyeDrawnInLayer
members.signature: public static StereoEye EyeDrawnInLayer(Camera camera, int layer)

docs.summary: The eye a layer of `camera`'s stereo view draws, which is the same eye in both for a camera drawing one.
